messages.content: I guess I'll look into getting a good one then. Do you think I should go for a higher capacity one, just in case?

That sounds like a solid idea. For observational setups, it's often safer to have extra "juice" on hand—it's always better to have extra power than to find your device dying in the middle of your session! A higher capacity battery means more hours of continuous use, which is great when you're deep into observation.

Just make sure to check the specific power requirements of your specific gear; a higher capacity battery won't necessarily mean *better* performance, but it will certainly ensure you won't have to worry about a power-out-of-the-way situation during the whole session!
I'll keep that in mind. Maybe I should also look into a backup power source just in case. What do you think?

That sounds like a very smart, cautious approach. Having a backup source—like a small power bank or a smaller portable charger—is always wise when you're out in the field, just in case your main gear hits a unexpected battery drain.
I guess I'll pick up a power bank then. It's better to be safe than sorry. Let me check if there's anything else I should consider.

result.content: Sounds like a sensible plan. Having a backup power source is a great move for when you're out and about! Do you know what kind of device you're planning to use the power bank with—is it for a specific piece of equipment, or a general use?"
